source_checks.notes: Reviewed the publication metadata, campaign scope, all three chain descriptions, the Attack Chain 1 ftp.exe/!more/cmd sequence, scheduled-task and curl commands, reconnaissance/upload behavior, conclusion and stated attribution basis.
Reviewed the DeviceProcessEvents purpose, MDE prerequisite, child and initiating-process fields, process unique identifiers and the documented Timestamp/DeviceName/ReportId event identity guidance.
Reviewed the FTP ! semantics, syntax, legacy Windows applicability and last-updated date; the version-scope limitation is stated in the report and validation plan.
Reviewed the Windows Command Shell technique definition and used it only to support T1059.003 for the source-documented cmd.exe execution.

mechanism.rationale: Section 2 and PDF page 3 identify the attacker-controlled LNK/script input, ftp.exe interpreter, documented ! trust-boundary transition, cmd.exe capability, inherited privilege context and the unverified EDR representation without treating the feature as a vulnerability.

timeline.rationale: Section 3 and PDF pages 2-3 distinguish the 2026-11-02 publication, 2026-11-03 analysis and source-stated several-month campaign period, then use a supported relative sequence because exact event dates and timezone were not disclosed.

root_cause.rationale: Section 2 and PDF page 3 correctly identify LNK execution plus the documented FTP ! facility as enabling conditions and explicitly retain the initial delivery vector, victim interaction and current-build behavior as unresolved rather than inventing a root cause.

execution_flow.rationale: Section 3 and PDF page 3 provide a causal five-stage flow from LNK execution through the FTP shell transition, cmd interpretation and separately scoped persistence/retrieval and discovery/transfer, with privileges and proof boundaries preserved.

impact.rationale: Section 4 and PDF pages 2 and 8 separate source-observed commands and vendor-stated campaign impact from possible command-execution consequences, reject privilege-escalation inference and avoid applying PapRAT capabilities to the FTP-only observable.

evidence.rationale: Section 5 and PDF pages 4 and 8 map campaign facts, official command semantics, schema and ATT&CK to C###/S### ledgers; they isolate the parent-child inference, single-source dependence, legacy documentation limitation and absent raw/lab evidence.

lab_plan.rationale: Section 7, validation.md and PDF page 7 specify authorized Windows/MDE environment and versions to record, logging, a harmless positive, three negative controls, expected artifacts, success/rejection/failure criteria, cleanup and the explicit not-executed state.
